A quartz crystal oscillator operates based on the piezoelectric effect and exhibits two closely spaced resonant frequencies due to its mechanical vibration modes and electrical equivalent circuit (RLC components).  
The equivalent circuit includes a series RLC branch (motional arm) representing the series resonance, and a parallel capacitance (due to electrode and holder) that combines with the motional inductance to create a parallel (anti-resonance) frequency.  
Thus, both series and parallel resonant frequencies exist, with the oscillation occurring at a frequency between them depending on circuit load conditions.  

Options (A) and (B) are incorrect because the crystal inherently has both resonances.  
Option (D) is incorrect because it denies the existence of either resonance, contradicting the piezoelectric resonator model.  

Final answer: (C)
